A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RPS research work. Their main text, equations, algorithms, figures and complete appendices support comparison. Relocated and renumbered appendix material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 7 and the appendices report original image-classification experiments measuring certified reliability, coverage, prediction-set size, runtime and ablation outcomes.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds experiments comparing pretrained and randomly initialized classifiers in Appendix B, Figure 11.

M1.justification: The hash-partitioned training, softmax-smoothed voting scores, majority prediction sets and certification algorithms remain unchanged. Clarified determinism, corrected notation and experiments with pretrained classifiers do not establish a redesigned RPS procedure.

E1.justification: Evaluation remains image classification on SVHN, CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 under training, calibration and combined poisoning. Figure 11 introduces ImageNet-pretrained classifiers evaluated on retained CIFAR datasets; it changes model initialization and training protocol without adding an ImageNet benchmark or a different prediction task.

E2.justification: The corresponding HPS and APS comparisons retain their comparator membership, including randomized, nonrandomized and reproducible APS. Figure 11 compares initialization variants within RPS; no additional competing prediction-set or certification method is evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds a fine-tuning-versus-training-from-scratch protocol using ImageNet-pretrained classifiers. Figure 10 extends the calibration-partition sweep to larger counts. The existing calibration/test split, ResNet architectures, optimizer settings and training budget remain stated as before.

E4.justification: New Figure 11 tests whether pretraining mitigates partitioning-related utility loss, examining CIFAR100 set sizes and CIFAR10 reliability. The extended Figure 10 sensitivity analysis reveals declining size reliability at large partition counts. Existing softmax, architecture, APS and statistical-efficiency analyses are retained; the last is relocated from Appendix C to B.1.

E5.justification: Both versions report five model initializations evaluated on five calibration splits, with means and standard-deviation shading. The statistical-efficiency experiment still uses 100 repetitions. Revised curves and uncertainty values do not introduce a different statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Numerical results are revised across the principal and appendix evaluations. Under the same reported CIFAR10/ResNet18 configuration with 100 training and 40 calibration partitions, coverage reliability at rt=rc=3 changes from over 23% to over 31%, and average set size from 3.6 to 3.41. New pretraining experiments report CIFAR100 sizes of 42.96 versus 18.16 at 100 partitions. Appendix A replaces the reported 100-model CIFAR10 training time of 21.7 hours with 2.4 hours. These are revised or newly reported measurements, not evidence of a demonstrated algorithmic speedup.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and the minimum-calibration-size proof correct the finite-sample quantile level from floor(alpha(n+1)-1) to that quantity divided by n. Section 5.2 corrects the partition-size definition. Theorem 2 is restated around disjoint calibration partitions and its independence argument is revised, while retaining the existing binomial reasoning. No new reliability theorem replaces the retained certificates.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the central claims of efficient RPS construction, pointwise reliability certificates under training and calibration poisoning, and empirical utility on image classification. Adding 'pointwise' in the conclusion clarifies a scope already explicit in v2.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds an explanation for declining size reliability when calibration partitions become too small. It interprets pretraining as a partial remedy for partitioning-induced classifier weakness and explicitly limits those guarantees to fine-tuning data, excluding pretraining data. The existing large-dataset utility limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 promises a future code release; v3 supplies a project-page link and states that code, seeds and reproduction instructions are available. Appendix A newly specifies sorting within training partitions and computing normalization statistics before augmentation, and revises runtime information. Appendix C additionally discloses alpha=0.05 for the APS experiment. These disclosures do not establish changes to the earlier implementation.

R1.justification: v3 adds Vovk (2013), replacing an unresolved citation in the statistical-efficiency discussion. Appendix D more explicitly credits Gasparin and Ramdas for the independent-set majority-coverage argument while retaining the existing criticism of their threshold construction. The broader related-work positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 edits introductory and explanatory prose, clarifies terminology, adds a reproducibility statement and changes the publication header. Appendix B is reorganized, and the statistical-efficiency study becomes subsection B.1. The main section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the three-panel Figure 11, extends Figure 10's horizontal ranges, corrects Figure 8's radius labels and relocates appendix figures. It also introduces presentation errors: calibration-partition axes in Figure 9 are labeled kt, and Figure 12 repeats the combined-poisoning full-set panel where v2 Figure 11 displayed empty-set results.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the paper through focused pretraining evidence, a clearer account of partitioning limitations, correction of the finite-sample quantile formula, and improved reproduction and access information. These gains are limited by unexplained replacements of existing measurements and new figure-label and duplicated-panel errors. The revision provides a modest net improvement without substantially resolving the retained method's limitations.
